title: Finite Reliability Representations: Noise-Calibrated Belief-Space Covers for Reliable Decision-Making
summary: Physical sensing and actuation noise floors should inform how much belief resolution a decision-making system can reliably use. We introduce Finite Reliability Representations (FRR), a framework for covering belief spaces by reliability cells: regions within which the optimal action-value function Q*(b,u) varies by at most a tolerance epsilon, uniformly over actions. The framework is formulated on beliefs rather than states and uses a cover rather than an equivalence quotient, because approximate decision-closeness is not transitive in general.
